parsed.rationale: All three diagnosed issues are HYPOTHESIS_NEEDS_VIDEO with story_defect_confirmed=false. Video critic observations show the two source-time jumps are deliberate highlight compression with consistent scoreboard state (0-1) across cuts, and no omitted causal/game-state information was observed. The thin ending issue has no visual evidence for the unobserved seg_go_ahead_scoreboard segment, so it cannot be confirmed or refuted. No search candidate has FIRST_LIVE_VERIFIED or narrative_fit_status=REVIEW_SUPPORTED, so no search_add is permitted. No confirmed redundancy issue names a preferred_drop_segment_id. The existing cut is understandable per sampled frames; unobserved segments remain unverified.

story_first_trial.rationale: This proposal is the most compact and temporally adjacent to the equalizer window (6403.81s–6410.07s vs equalizer buildup at ~6442s). The three interceptions are all non-replay footage events and the observation query targets whether the final interception (event_000636) initiates forward progression toward the equalizer. This directly addresses the unresolved question of whether the buildup-to-equalizer transition has omitted causal state. Other proposals either rely on replay-flagged VAR footage (interval_01:H1), misattribute team sides (interval_01:H2, H4), or lack interleaved opponent events to support their claimed rhythm (interval_01:H3). Interval_02 proposals are weaker because they span post-equalizer to go-ahead with no verified same-phase linkage and several opposing-team actions.
